title: Hard floors hold at every rung
description:
One spec suite that runs every floor against every rung, including `publish_auto`: a machine never sets five stars and lists candidates for a person instead; nothing under three stars, unrated or only predicted reaches a public page or a notification; no 'Approved by' credit is ever written; third-party images are credited; a quotation hold or a translation hold stops that item; doubt (an error-level finding, a contradicted claim, a legal hit, the loop limit) stops automatic publishing and raises a hard gate; a machine never changes an existing concept, never resets a Reference a person decided, never overwrites a block a person pinned; no Message is written by a machine; spend stops at the budget.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every floor has a scenario at `publish_auto` that fails if the floor is lowered.
- The floors are in the gate, not in each agent.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- hard-floors.feature: one scenario per floor at the highest rung; a five from an agent is refused and listed as a candidate; an unrated item is not announced; doubt raises a hard gate on a fully automatic site.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Authorization: the autonomy ladder as configuration. Slice code E4 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
